9.21.23.en: For I am Your servant and the son of Your handmaid.

9.21.24.en: You carry me in Your hands to Your bosom.

9.21.25.en: You give me surpassing resources from Yourself!

9.21.26.en: * My soul praises You, who have chosen me for Yourself!

9.21.27.en: You have granted me to surrender to You my whole being, so that You make of me a holy temple, even my body becomes a spiritual tabernacle!

9.21.28.en: You created me for a mission from You.

9.21.29.en: Make known to me: what do You want me to do?

9.21.30.en: Lead me all the way by Your wisdom.

9.21.31.en: Without You I shall not know how to begin!

9.21.32.en: Without You I shall not continue in the work!

9.21.33.en: Without You I shall not reach the end!

9.21.34.en: * Sanctify my mind, that I may know Your will.

9.21.35.en: And sanctify my will, that it may be in harmony with Your will.

9.21.36.en: Work in me, that everything that does not please You may flee from me!

9.21.37.en: And let not the enemy of good be able to lead me astray, nor the love of the world to seduce me, nor the lusts of the flesh to break my spirit, nor the earthly tabernacle to weigh me down with cares.

9.21.38.en: * I cry out to You, O divine Wisdom, shine upon me with Your light, that my soul may be enlightened and perceive Your mysteries.

9.21.39.en: The doors of heaven will open before me, and I shall enjoy the sight of You.

9.21.40.en: You carry me to You, and I shall enjoy the fellowship of glory.

9.21.41.en: To You belongs salvation, O Savior of the world!

10.0.s.en: 1. The role of wisdom in the life of Adam

10.0.0.en: 1 She preserved the first-formed father of the world, when he was created alone, 2 and delivered him out of his fall, and gave him strength to have dominion over all things.

10.0.1.en: It was she who watched over the first one formed, the father of the world, after he was created alone, and delivered him from his fall. [1]

10.0.2.en: It is difficult to perceive the role of divine wisdom in protecting Adam while he was in the garden of Eden, but Adam's giving of names to the animals for the first time, without enjoying the experiences of predecessors (Gen 2:18-20), requires great wisdom and authority. Moreover, when Adam fell because of his disobedience, God did not forsake him but took up his cause, and the wisdom of God offered him the way of salvation.

10.0.3.en: * When Adam transgressed the commandment of God and obeyed the wicked serpent, he became sold, or sold himself, to Satan, and the soul, that sensible creation which God fashioned in His own image, was clothed with the soul of the wicked one like a garment. Therefore the Apostle says: "Having spoiled principalities and powers, he triumphed over them in the cross" (Col 2:15), and this is the purpose for which the Lord came (into the world), that He might cast them out and recover His house and His temple, that is, man.

10.0.4.en: St. Macarius the Great. * He loosed Adam, the chief of the captives, from his bond, for the Savior heard the voice of the prisoner, and came down and rescued him from under the earth, that He might raise him to the height of heaven.

10.0.5.en: St. Jacob of Serugh. As for his being "alone," perhaps it means that he is the only one whom God created from the dust and breathed into him the breath of life, while Eve came from his side, and their children were born of them. Or perhaps it means that he is unique, given authority over all creatures (Gen 1:26-28; Wis 9:2-3).: Some think that Adam, when he was alone, before the creation of Eve, who played her part in his temptation.

10.1.0.en: And gave him strength to have dominion over all things. [2]

10.1.1.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa looks upon man as a unique being, the object of God's surpassing love, whom He created, alone among all, in His image and likeness. He set him up as king... therefore He did not form him until after the creation of the whole world, as a royal palace for the beloved king, man! He created him to bear witness to Him by sharing His goodness, so that he bears fellowship in the divine attributes, especially love and holiness... as He also gave him authority. And when he fell by his own will, and chose evil, which is not the work of God but the absence of virtue, He did not leave him, but the divine Word came incarnate to restore to him his first image, and to bring him into sonship to God, and to return to him his paradisal state... He is the goal of God's work of salvation.

10.1.2.en: * All the world is well-ordered and awaits man; issue Your command, O working power, that he may come and take possession of his dominion.

10.1.3.en: * He placed over his head a lock of hair like a crown, that he might be known by his creatures to be a king.

10.1.4.en: * (Adam) stood alone as the image of [the Son], full of beauty, and the creatures feared the image and obeyed it; the likeness of the Son appeared in the heir who was formed, and the heights and the depths and all creatures submitted to him, the new Christ; Adam, who became an image of the Son, stood in the world, and all the world knelt and worshiped him.

10.1.5.en: The light longed for him, because the image of light was pictured on his face, and heaven rejoiced and its light hastened to serve him, the sea was glad and prepared its fishes to present to him, and the earth was pleased and knelt and worshiped with its trees, the sun and the moon offered him their rays, and by their rising they were adorning the new Lord, the new reptiles and what is in the waters, and the birds flying in the air, were worshiping him in pairs and pairs, and boasting of him, all the beasts and animals and the kinds that came to be bowed the shoulder to put the yoke on their necks, the possessions came before the owner in choirs and choirs, and companies and companies, and throngs and throngs, and pairs and pairs, they came worshiping, and full of trust and love, and the head of the wild beasts was bowed to submit to him, there was pictured on Adam the great image of divinity, and as soon as the world saw him all of it submitted to him, all the kinds of beasts and animals came forward, and worshiped him, and he set his seal upon his possessions.

10.2.s.en: 2. The role of wisdom in the life of Abel

10.2.0.en: 3 But when the unrighteous man departed from her in his anger, he perished in the fury in which he murdered his brother.

10.2.1.en: But when the unrighteous man departed from her in his anger, he perished in the fury with which he killed his brother. [3]

10.2.2.en: By the "unrighteous man" he means Cain (Gen 4:8-13), for because of his injustice to his brother and his shedding his blood he died spiritually (perished).

10.2.3.en: Cain's offering was rejected because of the impurity of his heart, and when Cain abandoned wisdom he was defeated by his anger, and brought upon his life misery and wretchedness.

10.2.4.en: In unwisdom Cain despised the life of his brother Abel, and behold, he despises God Himself in his speaking with Him. For every sin aimed at our brothers drives us to sin against God Himself. And as St. John Chrysostom says:

10.2.5.en: [Let none of us despise another, for this is an evil work that teaches us to make light of God Himself. In truth, if one scorns another, he scorns God, who commanded us to show every concern for others. Cain despised his brother, and at once made light of God.]

10.2.6.en: * You know, my dear, that the sign of an offering accepted by God is the descent of fire from heaven and the burning of the offering. When Abel and Cain offered their offerings together, the living fire that ministers before God (Ps 104:4) came down and consumed the pure sacrifice of Abel, while it did not touch the impure sacrifice of Cain. Thus Abel knew the acceptance of his offering and Cain the rejection of his offering. The fruits of Cain's heart were afterward made known when he was tested and his heart was found full of deceit, when he killed his brother, so that what he conceived in his mind his hands brought forth. But the purity of Abel's heart was the foundation of his prayer.

10.2.7.en: St. Aphrahat the Persian Sage. Cain committed a most hideous crime, and yet if he had sought the wisdom of God it would have removed his folly from him and he would have offered a repentance that would save him, as St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian says.

10.2.8.en: * God appeared to Cain with gentleness, so that if he repented the sin of murder that his fingers committed would be pardoned by the contrition of his lips. If he did not repent, a bitter sentence would fall upon him, in keeping with his wicked folly.

10.3.s.en: 3. Its role in the life of Noah

10.3.0.en: 4 And when the flood overwhelmed the earth because of him, wisdom again saved it, guiding the righteous man in a vessel of mean wood.

10.3.1.en: And when the flood overwhelmed the earth because of him, wisdom again saved it.

10.3.2.en: Guiding the righteous man by a paltry piece of wood. [4]

10.3.3.en: The righteous man here is Noah, who escaped the flood by the ark.

10.3.4.en: For the first time Holy Scripture mentions that the flood was a result of the evil that multiplied on the earth because of Cain, and that God preserved the world for the sake of righteous Noah and his family by means of a mean wood, that is, the ark, as a symbol of the Cross, the sign of shame and disgrace and curse among the Jews.

10.3.5.en: He attributes the flood to the unrighteous "Cain," since he reckons him an example, which the wicked imitated in the days of Noah. In Josephus the Jewish historian it is said that the wicked are the sons of Cain according to Jewish tradition, though this does not appear in Holy Scripture.

10.3.6.en: Attributing the flood to the sin of Cain seems to be a kind of exaggeration, but the writer looks to the hideousness of this sin together with God's long-suffering toward the descendants of Cain, and when the measure was full the flood came.

10.3.7.en: If the wicked, because they did not enjoy the divine wisdom, were corrupted in their evils and exposed to the flood, then Noah in contrast held fast to the wisdom of God, and so enjoyed the symbol of the Cross and the Church, that is, the ark, and was saved from destruction.

10.3.8.en: * That ark was a sign of the Church, the bride of Christ, which is His holy congregation, just as the ark was joined one part to another by Christ from many races and countries and tongues. Christ gathered them to faith in Him, and made all one by His Spirit, gathered together by His love and their keeping of His commandments like the gathering of the wood of the ship one to another by nailing and the laying on of pitch. Likewise the fear of Christ and His love in the assembly of believers who fear and love Him, and one another, and their being nailed together by spiritual love, and their union together by keeping the commandments, so that all may be one ark, one body of Christ. Each of them, as God has given him of the gifts, serves another who has not received them... God told Noah to lay on pitch inside and outside, that is, that love be within their hearts toward one another, cleansing their outside by their services and care and consolation of one another, nailed together with the nails of the fear of the Lord, and love covers them from the entry of Satan to them, as the pitch protects the ship from the entry of water.

10.3.9.en: And as the planks of the ship cannot be joined one to another except by nails, so the congregation cannot be gathered in harmony one with another except by the fear of Christ our God... And because the Church believes in the Trinity, he pointed to the mention of the Trinity in the ship, repeating on every side the three decks and the height of three hundred and thirty cubits.

10.4.s.en: 4. Its role in the life of Abraham

10.4.0.en: And when the nations conspired in evil and were put to shame together, it is she who knew the righteous man, and kept him blameless before God, 5 It is she who, when the multitude of the nations agreed together in evil, found the righteous man and preserved him for God without blemish, and kept his inward parts deaf toward his son.

10.4.1.en: And kept him stronger than his tender affection for his son. [5]

10.4.2.en: He refers here to the Babylonians who joined together to build the tower of Babel for fear that the flood would be repeated, so that they might escape it. They look to God as an enemy, and so wisdom turned aside from them, and they thought they were able to flee from God. They dealt with the matter by human wisdom instead of the divine wisdom that calls us to flee from the divine wrath by throwing ourselves into the bosom of God and enjoying His mercy through repentance. Their deprivation of wisdom drove them to shame, where their tongues were confused, and they were scattered in the world (Gen 11).

10.4.3.en: * The peoples and multitudes applauded with one opinion to begin the work of iniquity with a hard heart: Come, let us take possession of the land, and dwell in it with might, like a gathered host lest it be scattered over the lands, let us hold to one another lest we be lost in the countries. Let us become one people and not be called peoples on the earth, let us build a village that the flood will not overcome, and let us erect a building that the waves will not sweep away, let us begin with a work that the rivers will not pierce, and let us make a fortress that can deliver from the flood, let us build a tower such that if the waters come out upon the earth and strike it, their waves will not overthrow it, let us lay a foundation such that if the great sea opens it will not break it or harm it with the strong waves, let us make sure and build something new that will not fall, and if the deep opens it will not reach it, and by skill let us build a great fortress in the name of the dreadful might and let us go up to heaven, let us go up and be neighbors of the sun in its high place and let our dwelling be by it and near it, let us go up and settle in the course in which the moon works, and look upon the changing of the seasons as they revolve, come let us go up to the stars of light in their courses, and come let us make for ourselves a name more famous than theirs, come let us rise to where the powers pass, and let us be companions of the galaxy that bears the times, let us build a chamber that is a beginning and an end: there was not one like it and nothing equal to it will ever come to be on the earth, come let us make for ourselves a village that reaches to heaven, and dwell there in the place high above harms, let us make a wondrous ascent by means of our gathering, and by it let us go up from the earth into the air, let us leave the clouds and take dominion over a place above them, and let us leave the winds and then rise to the heights, let us make bricks and burn them with fire, and let us raise a building of stone that will not be destroyed.

10.4.4.en: St. Jacob of Serugh. In contrast to that, Abraham lived in the midst of pagan peoples, even his tribe worshiped the moon, but wisdom preserved him to be a father of all believers (Wis 10:5). By wisdom Abraham offered his son as a sacrifice to God, reckoning his love for God greater than his love for his only son, and so he enjoyed righteousness.

10.4.5.en: God gave man the mind as a divine gift that it befits him to sanctify for his edification in all aspects of his life. But the people of the land of Shinar abused the gift because they did not ask God's wisdom for their sanctification, and in pride they thought they were able to face God's disciplines by human ways. They wanted to set up a tower with its head in heaven, and they went down all the more to the abyss. A painful picture of him who rejects the wisdom of God and relies on his own human wisdom.

10.4.6.en: * See how evil are greatness and pride with wisdom! All were gathered and agreed. They magnified themselves, so God scattered them. Thus greatness scatters the company of all the boastful... The Lord came down to see their deed. Thus He prophesied beforehand of His coming down in the body for the sins of men at the end of time... He mentioned the coming down to the children of Israel to train them in it and lead them on step by step, so that they would not deny the true coming down in His incarnation.

10.4.7.en: St. Ephrem the Syrian. Here the wise man compares a people who relied in pride on their human wisdom, so they were scattered, with Abraham who believed in God and loved Him, and offered his only son as a burnt offering. Isaac returned with him, from whom came the One in whom all the nations are blessed.

10.4.8.en: * By faith Abraham did not hesitate when he offered his only son, in whom he had received the promises, for he reckoned that God was able to raise him up from the dead (Heb 11:17-19).

10.4.9.en: Thus the Apostle gives us a report of the thoughts of the believing man, that faith in the resurrection had been established at that time in Isaac. Therefore Abraham hoped for the raising of Isaac, and believed what would happen in the future and had not yet happened.

10.4.10.en: Now how can the children of Abraham not believe what is actually happening in Christ, when Abraham believed that it would happen, and that in Isaac?

10.4.11.en: Rather, I speak more clearly: Abraham knew himself to be a symbol of the image of the coming truth.

10.4.12.en: He knew that Christ would be born of his seed, He who would be offered a true sacrifice for the whole world and that He would rise from the dead.

10.4.13.en: Origen. By the wisdom of God, and not by his own abilities or understanding, Abraham perceived the things to come as though they were present in his life.

10.4.14.en: * When Abraham offered his son Isaac, he was a symbol of God the Father, while Isaac was a symbol of our Lord and Savior.

10.5.s.en: 5. Its role in the life of Lot

10.5.0.en: 6 It is she who delivered the righteous man from the perishing ungodly; he fled from the fire that fell upon the five cities. 7 To this day a waste land that smoketh testifieth of their wickedness, and plants bearing fruit that never ripens, and a standing pillar of salt as a memorial of a soul that did not believe. 8 For those who neglected wisdom were not only deprived of knowing the good, but left to men a memorial of their folly, so that they could not hide the things in which they slipped. 9 But those who served wisdom she delivered out of every toil.

10.5.1.en: It was she who delivered the righteous man when the wicked perished, as he fled from the fire that fell upon the five cities. [6]

10.5.2.en: The righteous man here is Lot, and the five cities, the Pentapolis, which are in the plain, are: Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela or Zoar (Gen 14:2).

10.5.3.en: St. Jerome has a beautiful comment on the character of Lot, for he says that since Lot's faith was little he went to Zoar and so saved a small town from destruction, and if he had greater faith he would have saved more and larger cities.

10.5.4.en: Wisdom delivered Lot from the fire that fell and the smoke that rose from the five cities, from which none escaped except Zoar, which God spared so that Lot might dwell in it. And when his wife lost wisdom she looked back, and became a pillar of salt.

10.5.5.en: Philo the Jew of Alexandria mentions that even in his days the place still gave off smoke, and it is likely that it was at the southern end of the Dead Sea where a chain of mountains extends for a distance of 8 km, on most of which salt is piled up, and called the mountains of Sodom, and there are to this day some pillars of salt, one of which is called Lot's wife.

10.5.6.en: Lot lived in Sodom, whose people were marked by evils and corruption, and as Peter the Apostle says: "And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: for that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds" (2 Pet 2:7-8). He was dwelling in their midst, but he was fleeing from them in his heart so as not to share in their iniquities. Therefore when Lot went out he never thought of looking back toward the people of Sodom. He fled from their evils, and consequently fled from the fire that fell upon them. St. Ambrose urged us to follow his example, fleeing from the love of the evil world and from indulgence in evil.

10.5.7.en: * Let us flee like Lot, who feared the crimes of the people of Sodom more than the punishments that came upon them.

10.5.8.en: * Certainly the holy man chooses to shut his house before the men of Sodom, and to flee from the contagion of their transgressions. When he dwelt with them he did not become acquainted with them, for he did not know their evils, and he fled from their shame. When he fled he did not look back toward them, since he did not wish to share with them.

10.5.9.en: He who withdraws from vices and renounces the way of life of his (wicked) fellow citizens is in a state of flight like Lot. Such a man does not look back, but enters the upper city through the paths of his thoughts, and does not withdraw from it until the death of the high priest who bears the sins of the world.

10.5.10.en: Truly He (our Christ the high priest) died once, but He dies for every person who is baptized into the death of Christ, so that we may be buried together with one another with Him, and rise with Him, and walk in newness of life (Col 2:12; Rom 6:4).

10.5.11.en: Your flight is good if your heart does not act upon the counsel of sinners and their way. Your flight is good if your eyes flee from seeing the cups and drinking vessels, so that they do not become fixed, longing for wine. Your flight is good if you do not answer the fool according to his folly (Prov 23:33) LXX. Your flight is good if your steps are far from the ways of the foolish. Truly man soon turns aside by evil counsels, but if you wish your flight to be good, let your ways be far from their words.

10.6.0.en: St. Ambrose. To this day a waste land that smoketh testifieth of their wickedness, and plants bearing fruit that does not ripen in its season, and a standing pillar of salt as a memorial of a soul that did not believe. [7]

10.6.1.en: Smoke: perhaps because of the haze or the light mist rising from the basin of the Dead Sea, or the heat because of the continental climate.

10.6.2.en: As for this plant, Josephus refers to it, and calls it the apple of Sodom, a plant that appears in that region and looks to the eye as if it can be eaten, but inside it is a black powder that cannot be eaten.

10.6.3.en: St. Ambrose says that Satan and Sodom are both behind man, so the believer must look forward, not backward, until he reaches the mountain with Lot and does not become a pillar of salt like his wife.

10.6.4.en: Origen sees in Lot a symbol of the soul earnest in its salvation which looks forward, while his wife symbolizes the body that wishes to hinder the soul from its spiritual longings and earnestness.

10.6.5.en: * When the soul walks toward salvation, the body looks back, and seeks pleasures. The Lord also said of this: "No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God" (Lk 9:62). He adds: "Remember Lot's wife." For truly she became a pillar of salt, appearing as a clear sign of folly. The salt represents the wisdom which she lost.

10.6.6.en: Origen. * God looks precisely at the real inner goal, like the wife of Lot, who alone with her whole will had inclined toward the evil of the world. He left her rigid and without feeling and made her like a pillar of salt, and left her without strength, unable to move, like a statue, but not without benefit, for she became (an example) so that those who have spiritual perception may be salted.

10.7.0.en: St. Clement of Alexandria. And those who turned aside from wisdom were not only harmed by not knowing the good, but left behind them for the world a memorial of their folly, so that they cannot hide their stumblings. [8]

10.8.0.en: But wisdom delivered her servants out of their toils. [9]

10.8.1.en: After mentioning examples of the work of wisdom in the lives of men from Adam to Lot, and the effect of being deprived of her, he gave in verses 8 and 9 a discourse on the danger of lacking wisdom, which arises from folly, and how wisdom delivered her servants from their toils.

10.8.2.en: On this pattern there came in the Constitutions of the Apostles a discourse of St. James the son of Zebedee, much like a prayer to God, in which he declares the blessings of the work of God's (wisdom) in some men of the Old Testament and the destruction of him who avoids her:

10.8.3.en: [You are the eternal knowledge, the perpetual insight, the unbegotten hearing, the natural wisdom... You subjected all creation to him (Adam) and gave him freedom to bring food for himself by his sweat and toil, while it is You who made the fruits of the earth sprout and grow and ripen... You called him to be reformed again and to loose the bonds of death, and You promised him life after the resurrection. Not him alone, but when he grew in abundance to an innumerable multitude, those who continued with You You glorified, and those who denied You You punished.

10.8.4.en: While You accepted the sacrifice of Abel (Gen 4) as that of a holy man, You rejected the gift of Cain, the killer of his brother, as that of a wretched and hateful one.

10.8.5.en: Besides this You accepted from Seth and Enosh (their gift), and translated Enoch, for You are the Creator of men and the giver of life and the support of the needy and the giver of laws and the rewarder of those who keep them and the chastiser of those who disobey them.

10.8.6.en: It was You who brought the flood upon the world because of the multitudes of the wicked (Gen 6-7), and saved righteous Noah from the flood by the ark (1 Pet 3:20) with eight souls, where was the end of a former generation and the beginning of a later one.

10.8.7.en: It was You who kindled a terrible fire against the five cities of Sodom and turned the fruitful land into a salt lake for the wicked who dwelt there (Wis 10:6; Gen 19; Ps 107:34). But You snatched Lot the holy man from the great burning.

10.8.8.en: It was You who delivered Abraham from the evil of his forefathers, and made him heir of the world, and revealed to him Your Christ, and appointed Melchizedek as a high priest to present worship to You (Gen 12 etc.).

10.8.9.en: It was You who compensated Your patient servant Job, the conqueror of the serpent, which represents evil.

10.8.10.en: It was You who made Isaac a son of the promise, Jacob a father of twelve sons...]

10.9.s.en: 6. Its role in the life of Jacob

10.9.0.en: 10 It is she who guided the righteous man, when he fled from his brother's wrath, in straight paths, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him knowledge of holy things, and made him prosper in his labors, and multiplied the fruits of his works. 11 In the covetousness of those who oppressed him she stood by him and made him rich, 12 and defended him from his enemies, and kept him safe from those who lay in wait for him, and gave him victory in a hard fight, that he might know that godliness is mightier than all things.

10.9.1.en: It was she who guided the righteous man, fleeing from his brother's wrath, in straight paths, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of holy things, and made him prosper in his labors, and multiplied the fruit of his works. [10]

10.9.2.en: The wise man did not ascribe wisdom to Jacob when he used means of deceit to obtain the birthright and the blessing or to obtain a greater share from his uncle Laban, but he speaks of her when he met the wrath of his brother Esau with a spirit of humility and generous giving.

10.9.3.en: By wisdom he enjoyed the opened heaven and the comforting heavenly visions, in return for Esau's hatred of him and attempt to kill him.

10.9.4.en: He refers here to the dream of Jacob, fleeing from the face of Esau his brother (Gen 27:41-28:17), where he saw heaven as the "kingdom of God," an evangelical expression rarely used in the Old Testament. Jacob enjoyed an eschatological vision, where God reigns over the believers, and establishes from them His divine kingdom.

10.9.5.en: "Holy things": points to the heavenly sanctuary or to the heavenly ones who are holy in the Lord.

10.9.6.en: * Consider an ascetic (Jacob); he was running, fleeing from an exceedingly violent man, he was fleeing from his brother, and he found his help in a stone, and this stone is Christ. This stone is a help to all who suffer persecution, but to the unbelieving Jews it is a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence (Rom 9:33; 1 Pet 2:8; Isa 8:14; 28:16). There Jacob saw a ladder set up on the earth with its top reaching to heaven, and in heaven the Lord leaning upon it, and he saw angels ascending and descending (Gen 28:12-13). Look, he saw angels ascending, he saw Paul ascending. And he saw angels descending, Judas the traitor falling headlong. He saw angels ascending, he saw saints ascending from earth to heaven, and he saw angels descending, Satan and all his army cast down from heaven.

10.10.0.en: St. Jerome. And gave him victory over the covetousness of those who oppressed him, and made him rich. [11]

10.11.0.en: And defended him from his enemies, and kept him safe from those who lay in wait for him, and gave him victory in a hard fight, that he might know that godliness is mightier than all things. [12]

10.11.1.en: Here he refers to the period of his service to his uncle Laban, who exploited him and deceived him and was covetous to send him away empty. As for his enemies, they are Esau and his men or Laban and his brothers (Gen 31:23).

10.11.2.en: By the hard fight he means his struggle at the crossing of the ford of Jabbok, striving with God (Gen 32:22-29).

10.11.3.en: Jacob's weapon in his battle and hard fight is godliness, which is mightier than all things.

10.11.4.en: The wise man tells us of our father Jacob, who in the midst of his toils found a stone to put under his head. What is this stone but the wisdom of God incarnate, on whom we lean our heads that He may sanctify them, and lift our thoughts to heaven amid our troubles in this world? Thus "wisdom delivered her servants out of their toils" [9].

10.11.5.en: * The stone under his head was Christ. He had not put a stone under his head before, but only when the time came in which he was fleeing from his persecutor. When he was in his father's house and enjoyed the comforts of the body, he had no stone for his head. But he left his home poor and alone, went out with nothing but a staff, and immediately in that very night he found a stone and put it under his head.

10.11.6.en: St. Jerome. * We have not read of the blessed Jacob that he set out with horses or asses or camels, but we only read that he carried a staff in his hand...

10.11.7.en: Jacob showed his staff to take a wife for himself (Gen 32:10), and Christ carried the wood of the Cross to save the Church.

10.11.8.en: When Jacob slept he put a stone under his head and saw a ladder reaching to heaven, while the Lord leaned upon the ladder.

10.11.9.en: Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles. * The ladder set up on the earth and reaching to heaven is the Cross of Christ, through which He granted us to reach heaven, and indeed leads to heaven. This ladder contains various steps of virtues, by which we rise toward heaven. Faith and righteousness and purity and holiness and patience and godliness and all the rest of the virtues are the steps of this ladder.

10.11.10.en: St. John Chrysostom. God gave Jacob intelligence, and he was able to debate with his uncle who had deceived him, but Jacob was exposed to danger when his uncle pursued him with his relatives who were with him. Here human wisdom could not have preserved Jacob, but God Himself intervened, and warned Laban not to do Jacob harm (Gen 34:24 etc.).

10.11.11.en: * Wonderful is the goodness of the Lord. For when God saw Laban determined to fight him and to enter with the good man into battle, He said to him, as one asking him to review his intention: "Take heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad" (Gen 31:25). He says to him: Do not try to trouble Jacob, not even with a harsh word, but take heed to yourself, review your evil attack, restrain your anger, bridle your raging thoughts... I ask you to note the compassion of God. Instead of God commanding Laban to return to his place, He was content to direct him not to use harsh and violent words with the good man. What is the reason for that? That the good man might learn and experience how far God's care for him extends.

10.11.12.en: Do you not see that if Laban had turned back, how could the good man and his wife have known this? God allowed Laban to go and bear witness with his lips to the words that were spoken to him by God... This truly is the sign of the creative wisdom of God, that He turns the enemies of the truth themselves into witnesses to the truth, so that they fight with their mouths on the side of the truth.

10.11.13.en: St. John Chrysostom. * Jacob, who purified his heart from all appearances, showing conduct full of peace, first sent away all his possessions and remained behind, and wrestled with God (Gen 32:23-25). For he who leaves worldly things draws near to the image and likeness of God. What is the wrestling with God but entering into a struggle for virtue, and he who strives with one stronger than himself comes to a better state by imitating God more than others? Since Jacob's faith and consecration were unconquerable, the Lord declared to him His divine mysteries by touching the hollow of his thigh (Gen 32:26). For of his seed the Lord Jesus was born of a virgin, and Jesus is not unlike God (the Father) nor less than He.

10.11.14.en: St. Ambrose. By divine wisdom Jacob strove with God and men and prevailed. He wrestled until the dawn, when the light of the Sun of righteousness began to rise upon him. The reward he received is the desire of the heart of every true believer, for he was no longer called Jacob, which means "he who pursues," but "Israel," which means "seeing," and as St. Augustine says: "a great name carrying a great blessing."

10.11.15.en: * The Lord says in the Gospel: "the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force" (Mt 11:12)... He says to Jacob: "Let me go, for the day breaketh," he answered him: "I will not let thee go, except thou bless me." And He blessed Jacob; how? By changing his name... See, it is one man, on one side touched and withered (Jacob), and on the other side blessed to receive strength (the seeing of God).

10.11.16.en: St. Augustine. St. Cyril the Great sees that as long as we are in the night of this world we wrestle, but when the dawn of eternity comes there is no more room for wrestling but for seeing God.

10.11.17.en: * You see how he did not continue in the wrestling at the beginning of the day. In fact there is no wrestling for those who have already lived in the light. Those who have come to such greatness it befits to say: "O God, my God, I watch for thee from the light" (Ps 62:2) LXX. And also: "In the morning thou wilt hear my voice, I will wait for thee, and thou wilt see me" (Ps 5:4) LXX. When the light of righteousness, that is Christ, rises in our minds and presents His brightness in our hearts, then we wait as noble souls, and are made worthy of the divine care: "The eyes of the LORD are upon the righteous" (Ps 34:15). At dawn the wrestling ceases.

10.12.s.en: 7. Its role in the life of Joseph

10.12.0.en: 13 It is she who did not forsake the righteous man when he was sold, but kept him from sin, and went down with him into the pit. 14 And in bonds she did not leave him, until she brought him the scepter of the kingdom, and authority over those who held him in subjection, and showed those who accused him to be liars, and gave him everlasting glory.

10.12.1.en: It was she who did not leave the righteous man whom they sold, but rescued him from sin, and went down with him into the pit. [13]

10.12.2.en: Since Joseph committed himself to wisdom in a spirit of godliness, she delivered him from the pit, and rescued him from the enticements of Potiphar's wife and sustained him in prison, and brought him up to the throne, and gave him great glory!

10.12.3.en: Joseph did not learn human wisdom and magic, but by godliness he overcame the wise men and counselors and magicians, and became a witness to the work of the wisdom of God in a foreign land! He became by his conduct and behavior a teacher of wisdom to the elders (Ps 105:17-22).

10.12.4.en: What does the wise man mean by saying that "wisdom did not forsake the righteous man [13], and did not leave him [14]"?

10.12.5.en: When righteous Joseph was sold and when he was put in bonds, wisdom was with him, for he was a symbol of the Lord Christ who was sold as a slave through the betrayal of His disciple Judas, and was put in bonds when He was brought to trial. The life of this righteous man bears a wonderful image as a symbol of the Lord Christ in many respects; it is enough for me to mention what St. Aphrahat wrote as an example of what is found in the writings of the Fathers on this matter.

10.12.6.en: * Joseph was persecuted, and his brothers were the persecutors. Joseph was glorified, and his persecutors bowed down to him, and his dreams and visions were fulfilled.

10.12.7.en: Joseph the persecuted was a symbol of Jesus the persecuted.

10.12.8.en: Joseph's father clothed him with a coat of many colors, and Jesus' Father clothed Him with a body from the Virgin.

10.12.9.en: Joseph's father loved him more than his brothers, and Jesus is the dear beloved of His Father.

10.12.10.en: Joseph saw visions and dreamed dreams, and the visions and the prophets were fulfilled in Jesus.

10.12.11.en: Joseph was a shepherd with his brothers, and Jesus is the Chief Shepherd.

10.12.12.en: When his father sent him to visit his brothers they saw Joseph coming and planned to kill him, and when the Father sent Jesus to visit His brothers they said: "This is the heir; come, let us kill him" (Mt 21:38).

10.12.13.en: Joseph's brothers cast their brother into the pit, and Jesus His brothers brought down to dwell among the dead.

10.12.14.en: Joseph came up out of the pit, and Jesus rose from among the dead.

10.12.15.en: After Joseph rose from the pit he had authority over his brothers, and after Jesus dwelt among the dead His Father gave Him a great glorified name (Phil 2:9), that His brothers might serve Him and His enemies be subjected under His feet.

10.12.16.en: After Joseph's brothers recognized him they were ashamed and afraid and amazed before his greatness, and when Jesus comes at the end of time and declares His greatness His brothers will be ashamed and afraid and tremble before Him because they crucified Him.

10.12.17.en: Moreover Joseph was sold into Egypt on the counsel of Judah, and Jesus was delivered to the Jews by the hands of Judas Iscariot.

10.12.18.en: When they sold Joseph he did not answer his brothers a word, and Jesus also did not speak nor answer the judges who tried Him.

10.12.19.en: Joseph was delivered by his master to prison unjustly, and Jesus was condemned unjustly by the children of His people.

10.12.20.en: Joseph gave up two garments, one in the hands of his brothers, and the other in the hand of his master's wife, and Jesus gave up His garments and they were divided among the soldiers.

10.12.21.en: Joseph, when he was thirty years old, stood before Pharaoh and became lord of Egypt, and Jesus, when He reached thirty, came to the Jordan to be baptized and received the Spirit and went out to preach.

10.12.22.en: Joseph sustained Egypt with bread, and Jesus sustained the whole world with the bread of life.

10.12.23.en: Joseph took the daughter of the wicked unclean priest as a wife for himself, and Jesus betrothed to Himself the Church from the unclean Gentiles.

10.12.24.en: Joseph died and was buried in Egypt, and Jesus died and was buried in Jerusalem.

10.12.25.en: Joseph's bones his brothers brought up out of Egypt, and Jesus His Father raised from the dwelling of death and He put on His body and ascended with it to heaven in incorruption.

10.13.0.en: St. Aphrahat the Persian Sage. And in bonds she did not leave him, until she brought him the scepter of the kingdom, and authority over those who held dominion over him, and she showed those who found fault with him to be liars, and gave him lasting glory. [14]

10.13.1.en: Wisdom accompanied him in his bonds to bring him into glory, so that instead of being a prisoner he became a man of authority, supplying with provisions those who held dominion over him, and perhaps he means here Potiphar and his household, and the jailer and those with him, and also his brothers who sought to kill him and sold him as a slave.

10.13.2.en: Some looked at him as a criminal thrown into prison, and counted what befell him as a sign of his evil and of God's wrath upon him, but the wisdom of God (God the Word) revealed his righteousness, and declared that his sufferings and afflictions were only for his glory in this world as in the world to come, for "she gave him everlasting glory."

10.13.3.en: * See how it suddenly happened that the prisoner became king over all Egypt; he who was sent to prison by the captain of the guard the king raised to the highest rank.

10.13.4.en: His former master looked, and suddenly saw that the man whom he had thrown into prison as an adulterer was rewarded by receiving authority over all Egypt. Do you not see the importance of enduring trials with thanksgiving? For this reason Paul says: "tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed" (Rom 5:3-5). Note: Joseph endured affliction with patience, and patience gave him experience, and experience worked in hope, and hope did not make him ashamed.

10.13.5.en: St. John Chrysostom. * What is the meaning of the ring that was put on his finger (Gen 41:42)? It is only that we may understand that the position of the episcopate by faith was granted to him so that he might seal others. And what of the robe but that it is the robe of wisdom? This alone is the excellence in wisdom which the King of heaven gave him. The chain of gold appears to represent good understanding. And the chariot (Gen 41:43) also points to the glorious heights for which he was made worthy.

10.13.6.en: St. Ambrose. * "They brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment" (Gen 41:14), then it was possible for him to enter in to the king. So he who was bound in the prison of sin, and a captive in the lusts of the world, far from God, cannot come to Him until he comes out of that unclean prison, that is, leaves the doing of sin, and shaves the superfluities of the hair of his head, which are the thoughts of his mind that love sin, and changes his raiment, which is his evil deeds, for good works. He who has cleansed his heart of evil thoughts in this way, and changed his sinful works for righteous works, is worthy to enter in to Christ, the King of kings, and to partake of His precious Body and Blood.

10.14.s.en: 8. Its role in the life of the people

10.14.0.en: 15 It is she who delivered a holy people and a blameless seed from a nation of oppressors. 16 She entered into the soul of a servant of the Lord, and withstood dread kings with wonders and signs. 17 She rendered to the saints a reward of their labors, and led them in a marvelous way, and was a shelter to them by day, and a light of stars by night. 18 She brought them over the Red Sea, and carried them through much water. 19 But their enemies she drowned, and then cast them up from the depth of the abyss upon the shore; so the righteous spoiled the ungodly, 20 and sang praise to thy holy name, O Lord, and with one accord praised thy hand that fought for them, 21 for wisdom opened the mouth of the dumb, and made the tongues of babes to speak clearly.

10.14.1.en: He concludes the whole book with an extensive discourse by which he shows how divine providence preserved the people through the events of the Exodus, as the most important event in the history of the people, as a symbol of the exodus that the world enjoys through the Crucified One. The writer showed the divine providence through examples that carry contrasts. This chapter came much like a sermon or a group of expository sermons on the Book of Exodus.

10.14.2.en: It was she who delivered a righteous people and a blameless seed from a nation of oppressors. [15]

10.14.3.en: After speaking of the work of the wisdom of God in the lives of individuals, to reveal His concern for every person, he speaks of the divine wisdom which delivers the holy people.

10.14.4.en: God calls His people "a holy people," "a blameless seed," because He sanctifies His people and cleanses them from every sin. And He calls Egypt, which subjected them and humiliated them, "a nation of oppressors."

10.14.5.en: Truly the world does not cease to embitter the life of the true Church with injustice in cruelty (Ex 1:14), but God cherishes her as His holy suffering Church, which is without blame, and calls her: "Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee" (Song 4:7). For she will not hear this praise from the divine mouth unless she shares with her Bridegroom, the wisdom of God, His sufferings and His crucifixion.

10.14.6.en: * The Bridegroom says: "I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense" (Song 4:6)... after Christ tasted death for sinners (Rom 5:8). Human nature was delivered from the stain of sin after the Lamb of God took away the sin of the world and destroyed iniquity (Jn 1:29). Therefore the Song says "Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee" and adds to that the mystery of the passion, which myrrh symbolizes, and then mentions the mixture of aromatic herbs and incense, which point to the divinity of Christ. He who shares with Christ in the myrrh will obtain the fragrance of the aromatic herbs and incense, for he who suffers with Him will receive glory with Him (Rom 8:17). And when he is in the divine glory he will obtain perfect beauty and be very far from every hateful blemish. By Christ and through Christ you are separated from sin. He died and rose from the dead for us.
